citations.claim: Initial total energy before close encounter
Energy already drifting as heavy pair closes to ~0.93
Energy drift accelerating as pair reaches ~0.63 with speeds ~10.9 and 1.9
First violation: energy jumped to -74.1, change 23.43 exceeds allowed 21.69, pair at 0.34 with speeds ~12.8 and 3.0

counterfactual.change: Same 5-body shrunk scenario but dt reduced from 0.03223 to 0.005 (one field); with finer timestep the same 7-step close encounter conserves energy and no rule is violated.

explanation: Fast close encounter of heavy bodies 2 (m~5.28) and 3 (m~14.77) with coarse dt~0.0322 (near dt max). Body 2 starts with vx~6.2 toward body 3; pair distance shrinks 1.44 (step3) -> 0.93 (step5) -> 0.63 (step6) -> 0.34 (step7) while speeds grow to ~12.8 and ~3.0. Fixed leapfrog with only 6 substeps per step cannot resolve the rapidly varying softened force at this separation/velocity, so kinetic (+504) and potential (-578) both blow up and their cancellation drifts by 23.4, exceeding the energy tolerance. Momentum stays exactly conserved, pointing to time-integration truncation error, not a force asymmetry. Reducing dt alone removes the failure.
vision_note: Two bodies at the bottom converge over steps 4 to 6 and appear to collide and overlap at step 7. All other bodies remain well separated and nearly stationary while this close pair undergoes the encounter.
